CTV-wwszGw8.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that urban noise comes mostly from motor vehicles, drawing on the book Curbing Traffic and a visit to Delft, a city that takes noise seriously.
CTV-wwszGw8.why: HN cites it constantly in threads on noise, EVs and car-free cities as the source that cars, not cities, are loud.

CZIINXhGDcs.summary: David Graeber's Talks at Google presentation on his book Debt: The First 5,000 Years, covering the history of debt, the myth of barter and the Jubilee tradition.
CZIINXhGDcs.why: HN recommends it as an 80-minute way to get the gist of the book and a different view of what money is.

C4VHfmiwuv4.summary: Everyday Astronaut's Tim Dodd runs an hour-long, data-driven analysis of what rockets actually emit and how that compares with airliners and other industries. It breaks down exhaust by propellant type, per-passenger and total emissions, and ways launches could be cleaner.
C4VHfmiwuv4.why: HN commenters cite it whenever rocket launch pollution comes up as a rebuttal to alarm, since it shows launches are small next to other sources.

C2RO34b_oPM.summary: Jiahao Chen's JuliaCon 2017 talk argues that vector transposes should be taken seriously in type systems and linear algebra libraries. It explains why treating vectors as matrices causes trouble in languages.
C2RO34b_oPM.why: Strongly recommended for anyone working with vectors for its clear take on how they should be treated in types.

CaCcOwJPytQ.summary: The first video in a 55-part series by Michel van Biezen that introduces the Kalman filter and builds from the rationale through algebraic examples to the full matrix treatment. The videos are short, blackboard-style lectures.
CaCcOwJPytQ.why: HN repeatedly recommends this series as a clear, step-by-step way to really understand Kalman filtering.

C25qzDhGLx8.summary: CGP Grey argues that aging and death are a problem worth defeating, using a short animated essay. It is part of a pair with a follow-up from Kurzgesagt.
C25qzDhGLx8.why: HN longevity fans point to it as a concise, fun statement of the case for fighting aging, and some say it changed their minds.

C_r5UJrxcck.summary: A one-minute IIHS demonstration crash test of a 1959 Chevrolet Bel Air against a 2009 Chevrolet Malibu, showing how much better the modern car protects its occupants.
C_r5UJrxcck.why: The go-to demonstration in car-safety debates that old cars were not better, showing crumple zones and a rigid passenger cell at work.

Cj4y0EUlU-Y.summary: An excerpt from the 1983 BBC series Fun to Imagine in which Richard Feynman describes how he and a mathematician friend counted in their heads in different ways, one verbally and one visually. It shows that people can reach the same goal through quite different mental methods.
Cj4y0EUlU-Y.why: HN points to it constantly in threads on inner monologue, visual versus verbal thinking and communication as the classic, entertaining demonstration that minds work differently.

CCOdQsZa15o.summary: Not Just Bikes explains missing middle housing, such as duplexes, townhouses and small apartment buildings. The video argues that zoning in the US and Canada has made these options almost illegal.
CCOdQsZa15o.why: Recommended as the standard short overview of missing middle housing and its link to zoning reform.

CaPgDQkmqqM.summary: Innuendo Studios' video from the Alt-Right Playbook series on how bad-faith actors control the conversation through debate tactics and moving goalposts.
CaPgDQkmqqM.why: HN recommends the series for explaining the tactics and mentality of bad-faith online arguments.

Cym4TZwTCNU.summary: Rich Hickey, creator of Clojure and designer of Datomic, gives a JaxConf 2012 talk that takes apart traditional database architecture. He presents a different way to think about databases and explains the reasoning behind Datomic's fact-based design.
Cym4TZwTCNU.why: HN points people to it as the clearest account of why Datomic is designed the way it is and of the problems with conventional database architecture.

CBYhVcO4WgI.summary: The opening lecture of the How to Start a Startup course at Stanford, with Sam Altman covering ideas and products and Dustin Moskovitz discussing why to start a startup.
CBYhVcO4WgI.why: HN commenters recommend the series as timeless startup advice from strong speakers, and cite specific points from Altman and Moskovitz.

C-kF25fWTO8.summary: James Trunk introduces Clojure syntax and thinking, covering its core data structures, immutability, the thread-last macro and live data analysis in the REPL.
C-kF25fWTO8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a clear, enjoyable introduction to Clojure and a good example of REPL-driven development.

C8--cXwuuFQ.summary: Christopher Domas's REcon 2013 talk on dynamic binary visualization for reverse engineering. He shows how rendering binary data as interactive visual maps and trigraphs reveals structure that hex dumps hide, leading to his Cantor.dust tool.
C8--cXwuuFQ.why: HN commenters say it permanently changed how they think about inspecting binary data, and point to it as the origin of visual binary analysis tools.

CJlrbMHLBd4.summary: Tim Hunkin's 1987 TV series episode on how vacuum cleaners and related household machines work, remastered and upscaled in 2021. It is part of the six-episode 'Secret Life of Machines' series with hands-on demonstrations of everyday technology.
CJlrbMHLBd4.why: Recommended as a clear, charming explanation of how machines work, including a demonstration of building an electric motor.

CK62I-4cuSY.summary: A four-minute Onion Talks parody in which a social media consultant pitches never putting any effort into social marketing. It lampoons TED-style talks and marketing consultants.
CK62I-4cuSY.why: HN commenters recommend it as the Onion Talks parody most relevant to tech and startup culture.

CKIye4RZ-5k.summary: Tech Ingredients shows how to build flat panel speakers from exciters and foam board, with construction guidelines, measured SPL comparisons and a complete system playing music.
CKIye4RZ-5k.why: HN commenters point to it as a build guide for cheap DIY speakers that sound as good as expensive ones.

CbIZU8cQWXc.summary: A short, music-driven video built from Neil deGrasse Tyson's remarks on why advancing the space frontier matters, contrasting NASA's small budget with war spending and stressing inspiration.
CbIZU8cQWXc.why: Recommended to anyone asking whether space exploration is worth the cost.

CjVQJdIrDJ0.summary: Daniel Kahneman's Talks at Google lecture on his book Thinking, Fast and Slow, covering System 1 and System 2 thinking and the psychology of judgment and decision making.
CjVQJdIrDJ0.why: Recommended as a one-hour substitute for the book's opening chapters for those short on time.

CpCrkO1x-Qo.summary: An Autoline After Hours episode with teardown expert Sandy Munro and a panel of auto journalists. It covers his Tesla Model 3 teardown, including the battery, drive modules, build quality and manufacturing automation.
CpCrkO1x-Qo.why: Commenters link it in Tesla threads as an informed, hands-on engineering view of the Model 3 and its manufacturing.

Cyya23MPoAI.summary: Norwegian climber Magnus Midtbo spends a day climbing with Alex Honnold on exposed routes, shot as a vlog. The video shows the stark contrast between Midtbo's visible nerves and Honnold's calm.
Cyya23MPoAI.why: Recommended for conveying viscerally just how exceptional Honnold's composure is compared to other elite climbers.

C27RVio2rOs.summary: Y Combinator CEO Michael Seibel lectures at Startup School on building a product people want: identifying the problem, the customer, an MVP and which customers to pursue first.
C27RVio2rOs.why: HN commenters point to it as practical YC advice on iterating on a product and talking to users.

C7-8nUU6e3E.summary: A roughly three-hour screen recording of designing a barebones STM32F4 board in KiCad, covering schematic, four-layer layout and routing, USB and a buck converter. It ends with ordering manufacture and assembly through JLCPCB.
C7-8nUU6e3E.why: HN people recommend it as a real, end-to-end PCB design walkthrough that beginners successfully imitated to learn KiCad.

CM0aohBfUTc.summary: Tom Nicholas critiques Veritasium's sponsored video on driverless cars, using it to examine YouTube sponsorships, science-channel credibility and how statistics and misinformation can be used in branded content.
CM0aohBfUTc.why: HN cites it in discussions of sponsored science content and Veritasium's credibility, usually as the go-to critique.

CUjt36SD3h8.summary: Fermilab's Don Lincoln explains why light travels slower in water and glass. He knocks down common wrong explanations such as absorption and re-emission, then gives the wave-mechanics reason tied to refractive index.
CUjt36SD3h8.why: HN commenters link it to correct the widespread misconception about why light slows in a medium.

CXv1j3GbgLk.summary: A DEF CON 20 talk by RenderMan on the security weaknesses of ADS-B, the unencrypted, unauthenticated aircraft tracking broadcast. It shows how easily the data can be spoofed and what that means for security designed in too late.
CXv1j3GbgLk.why: Cited whenever aviation or vehicle communication security comes up, as the standard demonstration that ADS-B is naively designed and trivially spoofable.

CaasbfdJdJg.summary: Mathologer uses continued fractions to show why the golden ratio is the most irrational number, comparing it with root 2, e and pi and pointing to where this shows up in nature.
CaasbfdJdJg.why: Recommended as a clear, visual explanation of continued fractions and why phi is hardest to approximate by fractions.

CbHjcwIoTiY.summary: A tour of the historic WLW transmitter facility in Mason, Ohio, recorded at Hamvention 2013. It shows the surviving equipment from the 500,000 watt AM era, when WLW was the only US station at that power, and explains the history.
CbHjcwIoTiY.why: Recommended as the definitive visual walkthrough of the WLW 500 kW transmitter, with detailed equipment views and lots of history.

C7JQ7Rpwn2k.summary: David Sachs of InvenSense explains how gyroscopes, accelerometers and compasses work on their own and together, demonstrated on a modified Android handset. He covers sensor fusion algorithms and why rotation math such as Euler angles matters.
C7JQ7Rpwn2k.why: HN recommends it as the definitive talk on mobile motion sensing, including why integrating acceleration twice drifts so badly.

CB-SCA1reqE.summary: A two-minute Rouxbe cooking-school demo of how to heat a pan properly before cooking. It uses the Leidenfrost effect, where water beads and skates across a hot pan, to show when a stainless steel pan is ready.
CB-SCA1reqE.why: HN people cite it as a practical test for pan temperature and as the way to get a stainless steel pan relatively non-stick.

Cfe5UQ-1L9Q.summary: Inigo Quilez live-codes the "Happy Jumping" animated scene in a Shadertoy GLSL shader over about six hours. He builds the raymarched character step by step, explaining the math and procedural techniques, with checkpoints linked for each stage.
Cfe5UQ-1L9Q.why: HN commenters point to it as a patient, full-length walkthrough of how a raymarched shader is built from scratch.

C1KT8PS6Zs4.summary: Destin Sandlin of Smarter Every Day explores molten glass and Prince Rupert's drops with a glass artist, including a process that freezes the moment glass shatters and an artisan who makes the drops.
C1KT8PS6Zs4.why: Commenters recommend it for the striking glass-shattering visuals and the artist's attitude of treating failure as a space for discovery.

CD0y-aU1sXo.summary: Eric Brechner, a Microsoft Xbox development manager, presents his Kanban approach for agile project management at Talks at Google. He covers using sticky notes to organize work, estimate and meet deadlines.
CD0y-aU1sXo.why: Recommended as a clear description of how Kanban works and a practical alternative to sprints.

CGRtyxEpoGg.summary: A design essay on why products designed in Western contexts often fail when deployed in developing countries. It covers expert blindness and cultural assumptions, with examples such as malaria nets and the One Laptop Per Child project.
CGRtyxEpoGg.why: Commenters cite it to explain expert blindness and the difficulty of solving problems from inside your own cultural context.

CPLdltN7wgE.summary: The author of lazygit demos 15 features of his terminal UI for git, such as staging individual lines and easier rebasing, aimed at making common git tasks simpler.
CPLdltN7wgE.why: Recommended as the author's own quick intro to lazygit, a TUI that makes git workflows more natural.

CS01Hmjv1pQ.summary: In an 11-minute TED talk, Ralph Langner explains how his team reverse-engineered the Stuxnet worm and worked out that it targeted industrial control systems, with a covert state origin. It is a compact look at cyber-forensics.
CS01Hmjv1pQ.why: HN points people to it as the short, accessible account of how Stuxnet was dissected, usually when Stuxnet or state-sponsored malware comes up.

CVxeuwlvf8w.summary: Computerphile with Professor Brailsford on how a 1979 Bell Labs team reverse engineered a Linotron 202 phototypesetter over a summer to get high-quality print output. It covers typesetting history and the later 2013 rebuild of the famous vacation memo.
CVxeuwlvf8w.why: Recommended alongside the original paper and Unix history threads as an engaging account of the typesetter hack.

CcAJ3_-Hou8.summary: Food YouTuber Adam Ragusea argues that gas stovetops are weaker than electric burners, dirty to clean, and a health risk from indoor air pollution. He cites Consumer Reports ratings and a literature review on gas stove health effects.
CcAJ3_-Hou8.why: Cited as an accessible overview of the case against gas cooktops in threads on cooking, induction and indoor air quality.

CcZdwX4noCE.summary: Tom Scott visits Penistone to explain the Scunthorpe problem, showing why naive web and profanity filters block innocent words.
CcZdwX4noCE.why: The go-to explainer whenever content filters wrongly flag innocent words, well made and short.

CesHr99ezWE.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on how century-old Supreme Court decisions left U.S. territories such as Puerto Rico, Guam and American Samoa without meaningful representation. It mixes comedy with a history of their legal status.
CesHr99ezWE.why: HN people use it as a quick, entertaining primer on territory status, citizenship versus nationality, and voting rights.

CnMRePtHMZY.summary: Technology Connections explains in 33 minutes why thermoelectric (Peltier) cooling is far less efficient than compressor-based refrigeration.
CnMRePtHMZY.why: It is the standard link whenever a new Peltier or thermoelectric cooling breakthrough is posted.

CuD7SCqHB7k.summary: Joe Duffy's RustConf 2017 closing keynote on his experience at Microsoft building Midori, an operating system written in a Rust-like safe systems language. He covers the technical and cultural challenges of applying those lessons to Windows.
CuD7SCqHB7k.why: HN repeatedly cites it for Midori lessons: compatibility matters for adoption, and the Windows team stayed sceptical even with Midori running real workloads.

CvRAqR2pAgw.summary: A short Bank of England video accompanying its 2014 Quarterly Bulletin article on money creation. It explains that most money is bank deposits and that commercial banks create new money by making loans, which simultaneously create matching deposits.
CvRAqR2pAgw.why: HN people use it as an authoritative, plain-English source from a central bank that loans create deposits, rather than banks lending out saved money.

Cwas_7H5KUs.summary: Glenn Gould's 1955 recording of Bach's Goldberg Variations, uploaded as a continuous performance of about 39 minutes.
Cwas_7H5KUs.why: Recommended as the best-known and most famous recording of the Goldberg Variations.

CxHa5KaMBcM.summary: Five hours of the late-night BBC Radio 4 Shipping Forecast, uploaded to mark its 150th anniversary. It can be used as sleep audio or to learn the sea areas named in the broadcast.
CxHa5KaMBcM.why: Offered as a calming, dry, familiar broadcast, fitting for a crowd that enjoys ambient and lofi radio.

C67Lh4LE5LY.summary: Louis Rossmann lays out evidence that a Yelp salesperson had friends leave negative reviews of his repair shop after he declined advertising. He frames it as extortion and defamation.
C67Lh4LE5LY.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence for claims that Yelp pressures businesses over advertising, mostly in threads about Yelp's practices.

C6nAxiym9oc.summary: Coffeezilla reacts to Sam Bankman-Fried's explanation of yield farming on the Odd Lots podcast, arguing he effectively described a Ponzi scheme. The video was made well before FTX collapsed.
C6nAxiym9oc.why: After the FTX collapse, commenters cited it as an early red flag, though others disliked the YouTuber's style.

C-52AI_ojyQ.summary: Numberphile explains the long and short scales for naming large numbers, covering millions, billions, trillions, milliards and the Greek myriad, with James Grime and Tony Padilla.
C-52AI_ojyQ.why: HN links it whenever a thread hits the ambiguity of whether a billion is 10^9 or 10^12.

C7H3V7tkxeA.summary: A 35C3 talk presenting a proof-of-concept SPI bus hardware implant with capabilities like those alleged in the Bloomberg Supermicro story, plus countermeasures for detecting such modchips.
C7H3V7tkxeA.why: HN cites it as a demonstration that the supply-chain implant attack described in the Bloomberg story is technically feasible.

CAOnSbDSaOw.summary: Robert Sapolsky's Stanford lecture on the limbic system as the emotional part of the nervous system, covering its role in decision making, links to the cortex and the functions of its subparts.
CAOnSbDSaOw.why: HN cites it as a real academic source to back up or correct claims about emotion, anger and anxiety in the brain.

CBrj4S24074.summary: Chris Crawford's 'Dragon Speech' from the first Game Developers Conference, in which he reflects on his dream for game design as an art form. This is a cleaned-up version of the old recording.
CBrj4S24074.why: HN people mention it as a notable historical talk from the early game industry, though some see it as showing his eccentricity.

CGAhWgkKlHI.summary: Technology Connections explains how refrigerator and freezer design affects energy use, using chest freezers to show why top-opening designs and layout choices matter. It includes thermal-camera footage of cold air spilling out of upright units.
CGAhWgkKlHI.why: HN points to it whenever chest fridges or freezer efficiency come up, as a clear explanation of design trade-offs between efficiency and convenience.

CGN4RFkhH2M.summary: Matt Wynne's GoRuCo 2012 talk on why Rails apps get hard to change as they grow, and how a ports-and-adapters hexagonal architecture separates application logic from the framework.
CGN4RFkhH2M.why: HN cites it as a resource for decoupling Rails code and for faster tests.

CIjXUg1s5gc.summary: T-Pain performs three songs at NPR's Tiny Desk, backed by only a keyboardist and showing his natural singing voice.
CIjXUg1s5gc.why: HN uses it as evidence that T-Pain can sing without Auto-Tune, so his sound is an aesthetic choice.

CJlqsdezhhk.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything segment arguing that US cannabis prohibition grew out of racially and politically motivated agendas under Nixon and earlier, rather than scientific evidence.
CJlqsdezhhk.why: Used as a pop-culture shorthand explanation for the political origins of drug laws.

CKh7UOELpPo.summary: John McCutchan of Google explains how Dart and the Dart VM expose SIMD instructions to speed up web software. He covers what SIMD is and how it applies to graphics and games.
CKh7UOELpPo.why: Pointed to as the original talk by the author of the SIMD-in-JavaScript proposal, whenever SIMD on the web comes up.

CLo3e1Pak-Y.summary: VICE News reporter Elle Reeve investigates China's rollout of facial recognition and mass surveillance technology and what it means for citizens. The report originally aired on VICE on HBO.
CLo3e1Pak-Y.why: Cited as a vivid demonstration of the scale of Chinese state surveillance, especially in TikTok and privacy debates.

CMR9z9Xr8GM.summary: Quint BUILDs tests a rooftop water storage setup in which solar power pumps water up to the roof and a turbine generates power later. He works through the numbers to show how much energy it actually stores.
CMR9z9Xr8GM.why: HN commenters cite it as an entertaining reality check on home gravity storage, showing the yield is tiny compared to household needs.

CX6LlEcJ4nw.summary: A Senate hearing clip in which Sen. Ted Cruz questions a Google executive about alleged political bias and censorship in Google's products. It is a short excerpt of congressional testimony from 2019.
CX6LlEcJ4nw.why: Commenters cite it as evidence in arguments about partisan bias at tech companies and as testimony worth watching.

CeDOQpfaUc8.summary: An Adam Ruins Everything comedy segment on why US hospitals are so expensive, covering opaque price lists, surprise bills and penalties for the uninsured.
CeDOQpfaUc8.why: Pointed to in healthcare cost threads as an entertaining primer on how the US system inflates prices.

CgASBVMyVFI.summary: Tom Lehrer performs his satirical song "National Brotherhood Week" with a spoken intro. The song mocks superficial displays of tolerance while prejudices between groups carry on.
CgASBVMyVFI.why: Mostly quoted or linked as a witty example of Lehrer's satire, often as a joke in unrelated threads.

CiHN0ZWE5bk.summary: Professor Mike Merrifield of Nottingham explains in a mostly uncut conversation why light travels slower in glass. He treats light as a wave and describes how the material's electrons produce secondary waves that combine to slow it.
CiHN0ZWE5bk.why: HN cites it whenever the popular absorb-and-re-emit explanation comes up, as a source for the wave-interference account.

ClfBxWPkBKU.summary: Former bank regulator William Black explains how fraud, including liar's loans, was committed from inside banks and drove the 2008 financial crisis.
ClfBxWPkBKU.why: Mentioned in threads about financial fraud as support for the claim that outright fraud, not just bad luck, caused the Great Recession.

Clgl63CWOkM.summary: Richard Ankrom's account of his 2001 guerrilla project, in which he painted and installed a missing freeway exit sign on a Pasadena freeway. The sign matched official standards and stayed up for years before being discovered.
Clgl63CWOkM.why: HN cites it as the best-known example of a citizen quietly fixing public infrastructure, often in threads on unsanctioned civic repairs.

CmZdGo6b5yA.summary: Tom Scott, with linguists Gretchen McCulloch and Molly Ruhl, examines whether the language you speak changes how you think. The short answer is mostly no, with caveats about the weak version of the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis.
CmZdGo6b5yA.why: Linked as a concise, accessible rebuttal whenever linguistic relativity comes up in a thread.

Cn4vC80Pv6Q.summary: A demonstration of the 1982 Xerox Star user interface, including its desktop, icons, documents, networking and printing. The uploader argues that Apple's later Lisa and Mac interfaces evolved from these ideas rather than copying them.
Cn4vC80Pv6Q.why: HN points to it as a look at an early GUI that did a lot with little learning curve, often to contrast it with modern software.

CnbVCNIh1NA.summary: A RacketCon talk presenting Fructure, a prototype extensible structured editing engine in Racket. Language providers define syntactic forms and refactorings as rewrite rules, and editing operates on program structure rather than on text.
CnbVCNIh1NA.why: Cited as a leading example of structural editing whenever threads discuss alternatives to text-based code editors.

CpfdtgW6_oI.summary: Paul Graham gives a keynote in his hometown of Pittsburgh, reflecting on the old and new city and arguing that it could become a startup hub.
CpfdtgW6_oI.why: Cited as the video version of his essay on making Pittsburgh a startup hub, and as a talk that persuaded at least one commenter to move there.

CtUfBc4qQMg.summary: A two-minute clip from the documentary The Fog of War in which Robert McNamara recalls Fidel Castro explaining how close the world came to nuclear war during the Cuban Missile Crisis.
CtUfBc4qQMg.why: Cited in nuclear-risk threads as evidence that Castro was ready to use nuclear weapons and accept the consequences.

CuoER1DwYLY.summary: Gamers Nexus builds a fully ray-traced demo in Unreal Engine to compare faked global illumination with RTX ray-traced GI. It covers the gains in dynamic scenes and accuracy against the performance cost and noise.
CuoER1DwYLY.why: HN uses it as a reference for how noisy raw real-time ray tracing is and how it compares with traditional faked lighting.

Cvq3Pf3j61c.summary: A two-minute clip from The Wire season 1 in which D'Angelo explains, using the McNugget, that having an idea does not get you paid. It is a short monologue about who profits from inventing something.
Cvq3Pf3j61c.why: HN posts it as a classic scene whenever threads touch on ideas versus execution or who captures the profit from invention.

CxVXvFOPIyQ.summary: Veritasium's long documentary on the history of Monsanto's herbicides, including glyphosate, and how patented seeds prevent farmers from replanting. It covers agricultural chemistry, litigation and corporate practices.
CxVXvFOPIyQ.why: Pointed to as a relevant, recent deep dive whenever Monsanto, GMO seeds or glyphosate safety come up.

CxwceUvxlCo.summary: A short Bookeen R&D demo showing real-time web page scrolling on an eInk panel, far faster than typical e-readers. It was a prototype for the next generation of Cybook readers.
CxwceUvxlCo.why: HN cites it as proof that eInk panels can refresh fast and that slow e-readers are mainly a display-controller problem.

C2vgICfQawE.summary: An animated, musical visualization of Conway's Game of Life showing patterns made in the Golly program.
C2vgICfQawE.why: HN commenters use it as an illustration of how simple rules can produce surprisingly complex behavior.

C3LFbOSPfrE.summary: An Empire Files documentary by Abby Martin presenting a critical account of the Afghanistan War, from the CIA's role in the 1980s to the stalemate of the 2010s and 2020. It argues the war was driven by imperial interests.
C3LFbOSPfrE.why: Mentioned only in passing, cited as support for claims that US interventions were driven by resources and that Western war reporting is biased.

C7TwBUxxIC0.summary: The Thought Emporium tests so-called negative ion and anti-5G wellness products and finds they are radioactive, with some coated in powdered thorium.
C7TwBUxxIC0.why: HN cites it as the debunking behind news stories about radioactive anti-5G pendants and wellness trinkets sold on Amazon.

CDeG4S-mJts.summary: A short parody clip in the 'Hitler learns about...' meme format, in which Hitler rants about git's confusing commands. It riffs on git's complexity and the Linus Torvalds and Facebook angle.
CDeG4S-mJts.why: Cited as a joke about git's notoriously esoteric interface, usually in threads about git or other Hitler-parody videos.

CHCCjlSWbHE.summary: Raw 1991 home footage of a working Etak Navigator, the 1985 in-car navigation system that predated consumer GPS. It shows the system's cassette-based map display and explains its augmented dead reckoning using wheel sensors.
CHCCjlSWbHE.why: Cited as a rare look at how pre-GPS car navigation worked, especially its dead reckoning with turn-based recalibration.

CHgUN_95UAw.summary: Lily Tomlin's classic 1976 Saturday Night Live sketch as telephone operator Ernestine, mocking the monopolistic Bell phone company with the line 'We don't care. We don't have to.' It is a one-minute parody of arrogant corporate indifference.
CHgUN_95UAw.why: Quoted as the go-to joke whenever a monopoly or big tech company ignores customers, from Verizon to Google to Apple.

CJXp3UYj50Q.summary: Dave2D reviews the Lenovo Legion Go S running Valve's SteamOS instead of Windows, calling it the first true competitor to the Steam Deck. He compares handheld gaming performance and experience across the two operating systems.
CJXp3UYj50Q.why: HN commenters cite it as reviewer evidence that games run faster and with better battery life on Linux/SteamOS than on Windows on identical hardware.

CMdHDHEuOUE.summary: A short Google video introducing the Quantum AI Lab, a partnership between Google, NASA, USRA and a 512-qubit D-Wave Two quantum computer. It covers the lab's early goals and some potential applications of quantum computing.
CMdHDHEuOUE.why: HN mostly cites it as a reference for the Google/NASA/D-Wave partnership and as a basic intro to quantum computing's potential.

CPNK0VspQ0M.summary: The 1990 Public Enemy song 911 Is a Joke from the album Fear of a Black Planet, about slow emergency response.
CPNK0VspQ0M.why: Commenters link it as a pun or ironic reference in threads about 911 and emergency services.

CPRvc2UMeMI.summary: A comedy song by onedeadtroll, from the Windows XP and OS X 10.3 era, lamenting that every operating system is bad. It features Wes Borg and Chris Smith.
CPRvc2UMeMI.why: HN quotes it as a joke whenever OS complaints and comparisons come up.

CQJgFh_e01g.summary: Adam Something argues that the Hyperloop is impractical, covering the costs and engineering problems of running trains in a near vacuum compared with conventional rail and metros. The description admits some wrong numbers in the original cut.
CQJgFh_e01g.why: Cited as a concise critique of Hyperloop feasibility whenever the idea comes up.

CRW0q8i3u6E.summary: A one-minute night drive along Mill Ave in Tempe, Arizona, filmed to show that the crash site looked much brighter than Uber's released dashcam video suggested. It was made in response to the fatal 2018 Uber self-driving crash.
CRW0q8i3u6E.why: Used as evidence that Uber's dashcam footage misrepresented how well lit the road was.

CS9ptA3Ya9E.summary: A sketch from That Mitchell and Webb Sound in which a caller learns that identity theft is, in effect, a bank robbery in which the bank blames the customer. It runs about two minutes.
CS9ptA3Ya9E.why: HN posts it as the obligatory joke link in threads about data breaches, credit bureaus and bank security failures.

CT7nnXej2K4.summary: A short Microsoft promo comparing classic Teams with the rewritten new Teams side by side, claiming faster startup and better performance. The new version is shown taking around nine seconds to launch.
CT7nnXej2K4.why: Not recommended; it is cited mockingly as an example of software bloat and of Microsoft calling a slow startup fast.

CZ3wIuvmHeM.summary: A QCon talk from Netflix on running a large microservices architecture and building resilience into it. It touches on tooling such as Hystrix and circuit breakers.
CZ3wIuvmHeM.why: Mentioned as a real-world example that microservices can work at scale, though commenters are lukewarm and unsure it matches what they remember.

CZrr7AZ9nCY.summary: A 2007 parody mocking Microsoft's Surface touch table, made by SarcasticGamer.
CZrr7AZ9nCY.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke when Microsoft hardware or large touch tables come up.

C_78DM8fG6E.summary: OpenAI cofounder Greg Brockman explains the design principles behind ChatGPT and demos unreleased plug-ins at TED 2023. In the follow-up, TED head Chris Anderson presses him on the timeline of development and the risks of releasing such a tool.

CqiL5QQnN64.summary: A Ray Summit 2022 keynote fireside chat between OpenAI's Greg Brockman and Anyscale's Robert Nishihara. They discuss how OpenAI's training infrastructure evolved and its use of Ray.

Cu-7UDT0Xe4.summary: A five-minute clip in which Erich Fromm asks whether the purpose of work is just making money. He argues that white-collar workers end up selling their personality, relating to others the way goods relate to each other on a market, and he points to creative pleasure, participation and usefulness to society as what work could offer instead.
Cu-7UDT0Xe4.why: HN commenters repeatedly cite it for Fromm's line about selling one's personality at work, especially in threads on careers, mental health and labor.

CzwtCBj5jEs.summary: An LGR Oddware episode looking at Sony's MDH-10 MD Data drive from 1995, which used MiniDisc for computer storage years before Hi-MD. The host tries out the drive with its original drivers and software.
